sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Scripts and libraries
sections.what: Lists the commands developers run (dev server, build, lint, typecheck, unit and end-to-end tests, database setup, data import and model fitting) and the libraries needed to build and test the app.
sections.why: Likely reason: one place for every command so nobody has to remember them.
sections.watch_out: Commands that load or change the database depend on helper scripts not shown in this packet.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Node version and override
sections.what: Says the app needs Node 20.9 or newer and forces the playwright-core package to version 1.56.1.
sections.why: Likely reason: the override keeps the browser library in step with the test runner.
sections.watch_out: The minimum is 20.9 but CI runs Node 22, so both must keep working after upgrades.

summary: The project manifest: names every command developers run and every library the app depends on, with version limits.
purpose: Be the single list of install, run, test, data and database commands.
why: This is the standard file for a Node project. Likely reason for the playwright-core override: it keeps the browser test library at the version the test runner expects.
how: 1) npm installs the listed dependencies. 2) Each script runs a command by name, often through a helper that loads settings. 3) The override forces one nested package to a fixed version.
inputs: Commands typed by developers, and settings loaded by helper scripts.
outputs: Installed packages and the results of each script.
risks: Caret version ranges let newer minor versions change behaviour. Several data and database scripts change the database, so their own safety checks matter.
debug: If install fails, check the Node version against the engines minimum. If a script fails, run its command by hand. If tests break after install, check the playwright-core override.
